prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
- Core stance: Founded in 1993, UKIP seeks UK withdrawal from the EU to restore sovereignty, democratic accountability and common law rights; keep the pound permanently; oppose an EU government/army/constitution; repeal the European Communities Act 1972 and replace EU membership with trade agreements.

- Economy: 
  - Free global trade beyond the EU, leveraging the Commonwealth and US ties; argue EU over-regulation harms competitiveness and SMEs.
  - Deregulation “bonfire,” prioritising small firms; simplify taxes (review CGT/IHT, restore married allowance, raise income tax threshold to lift 1m out of tax); consider replacing VAT outside the EU; oppose EU tax harmonisation.
  - Keep sterling; retain Bank of England independence.
  - “Independence Dividend” ≈ £20bn/yr from ending EU budget payments and gains from growth, bureaucracy cuts and fisheries. Planned uses: agriculture £2bn; regional support £1bn; pensions +£5/week (£2.8bn), elderly care £0.5bn, restore expat pensions £0.3bn; tax cuts £2.7bn; NHS £2bn + nurses £0.5bn; 30,000 teachers £1.2bn; 25,000 police £0.8bn; fuel duty cut 9p/l (£3.7bn); defence £2.5bn.

- Health, welfare, pensions:
  - Decentralise and de-bureaucratise NHS; restore “matron” model; raise nurse pay; prioritise patient care over management/consultancy; recruit internationally post-EU.
  - Simplify benefits to make work pay; consider basic income in limited cases; support families via tax; reduce fraud and admin costs.
  - Gradually shift to funded private pensions by diverting part of NI for younger workers; current pensioners protected.

- Education:
  - Emphasise basics; allow selection/streaming; cut class sizes (<25) via 30k more teachers; elevate technical/vocational routes; consider vouchers; curb political bias and EU “propaganda”; stop selling school playing fields; promote sport.
  - HE: reduce central micromanagement; diversify funding (loans to institutions, private universities, scholarships); end EU fee discrimination and EU-funded integration posts.

- Transport and environment:
  - Integrated transport; not anti-car; cut fuel duty; invest in roads, rail maintenance and cycling; RFL to favour low-emission cars; oppose Climate Change Levy; pragmatic approach to ownership/privatisation.
  - Decentralised, market-led environmental policy with strong local monitoring; protect consumers and organic farming from GMOs with clear labelling; oppose EU-driven animal testing expansion; support renewables (biofuels, wind, wave, solar, hydrogen).

- Home affairs, immigration, asylum:
  - Defend common law (jury trial, presumption of innocence); oppose EU Corpus Juris and Europol powers; repeal and re-enact Human Rights Act to fit UK tradition; reject EU Charter of Fundamental Rights.
  - More community policing and officers; deterrent sentences with rehabilitation for non-violent offenders; “life means life” for heinous crimes.
  - UK-controlled, skills-based immigration (Canada/Australia model); equalise treatment for Commonwealth families; faster, firm but fair asylum processing with monitoring/detention; prioritise first safe country; seek reform of 1951 Refugee Convention.

- Agriculture and fisheries:
  - Leave CAP; introduce voluntary Land Management Contract Scheme paying for environmental/public goods; extra support for less-favoured areas; promote organic and high animal-welfare standards; help young farmers; enable diversification; nuanced access to countryside; create a Department of Agriculture & Rural Affairs.
  - Leave CFP; assert exclusive UK control (to 200 miles); recovery zones and sustainable methods; bilateral access only.

- Defence, foreign affairs, constitution:
  - Increase defence funding; buy cost-effective US kit; exit EU Rapid Reaction Force; anchor policy in NATO and US ties; strengthen reserves and cadets.
  - Aid routed to communities, conditional on freedom and fiscal honesty.
  - New UK Bill of Rights barring any future cession of sovereignty; strengthen Parliament and Select Committees; curb quangos; oppose state party funding; restore county-based local government; wider use of referenda via petition; revisit Welsh settlement; no EU constitution to override UK law.
